Callers inspect\n// it with errors.Is; the wrapped message names the line that failed.\nvar ErrSyntax = errors.New(\"invalid TOML\")\n\n// Decode reads a TOML document from r and returns its tagged-value model.\n// Each top-level key maps to {\"type\", \"value\"} with the value as a string.\n// Only top-level key/value pairs with string values are decoded so far.\nfunc Decode(r io.Reader) (map[string]any, error) {\n\tdata, err := io.ReadAll(r)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"read document: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\tif !utf8.Valid(data) {\n\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"%w: document is not valid UTF-8\", ErrSyntax)\n\t}\n\tp := &parser{src: string(data)}\n\treturn p.document()\n}\n\n// parser scans src by byte offset. Multi-byte runes are copied through unchanged,\n// so the ASCII delimiters the scanner checks are never confused with them.\ntype parser struct {\n\tsrc string\n\tpos int\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) document() (map[string]any, error) {\n\tdoc := map[string]any{}\n\tfor {\n\t\tp.skipSpaces()\n\t\tif p.done() {\n\t\t\treturn doc, nil\n\t\t}\n\t\tif c := p.src[p.pos]; c == '#' || c == '\\n' || c == '\\r' {\n\t\t\tif err := p.endOfLine(); err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tkey, value, err := p.keyValue()\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t\tif _, dup := doc[key]; dup {\n\t\t\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"duplicate key %q\", key)\n\t\t}\n\t\tdoc[key] = value\n\t\tif err := p.endOfLine(); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) keyValue() (string, map[string]any, error) {\n\tkey, err := p.key()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn \"\", nil, err\n\t}\n\tp.skipSpaces()\n\tif p.done() || p.src[p.pos] != '=' {\n\t\treturn \"\", nil, p.errorf(\"expected '=' after key %q\", key)\n\t}\n\tp.pos++\n\tp.skipSpaces()\n\tvalue, err := p.value()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn \"\", nil, err\n\t}\n\treturn key, value, nil\n}\n\n// key reads a bare key or a single-line quoted key. Dotted keys and table headers\n// are not decoded yet, so a '.' or '[' is reported as a syntax error.\nfunc (p *parser) key() (string, error) {\n\tif p.done() {\n\t\treturn \"\", p.errorf(\"expected a key\")\n\t}\n\tswitch p.src[p.pos] {\n\tcase '\"':\n\t\treturn p.basicString()\n\tcase '\\'':\n\t\treturn p.literalString()\n\t}\n\tstart := p.pos\n\tfor !p.done() && isBareKeyByte(p.src[p.pos]) {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t}\n\tif p.pos == start {\n\t\treturn \"\", p.errorf(\"expected a key\")\n\t}\n\treturn p.src[start:p.pos], nil\n}\n\n// value reads a string in one of its four forms and returns its tagged model.\n// The longer delimiters are tested first so that `\"\"\"` is never read as `\"\"`.\nfunc (p *parser) value() (map[string]any, error) {\n\tif p.done() {\n\t\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"expected a value\")\n\t}\n\tvar s string\n\tvar err error\n\tswitch {\n\tcase strings.HasPrefix(p.src[p.pos:], `\"\"\"`):\n\t\ts, err = p.multiline('\"', true)\n\tcase p.src[p.pos] == '\"':\n\t\ts, err = p.basicString()\n\tcase strings.HasPrefix(p.src[p.pos:], \"'''\"):\n\t\ts, err = p.multiline('\\'', false)\n\tcase p.src[p.pos] == '\\'':\n\t\ts, err = p.literalString()\n\tdefault:\n\t\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"expected a string value\")\n\t}\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\treturn map[string]any{\"type\": \"string\", \"value\": s}, nil\n}\n\n// endOfLine consumes trailing spaces, an optional comment, and the line break.\n// End of input also ends a line.\nfunc (p *parser) endOfLine() error {\n\tp.skipSpaces()\n\tif !p.done() && p.src[p.pos] == '#' {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t\tfor !p.done() && !p.atNewline() {\n\t\t\tif isDisallowedControl(p.src[p.pos]) {\n\t\t\t\treturn p.errorf(\"control character in comment\")\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tp.pos++\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif p.done() {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\tif p.src[p.pos] == '\\n' {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\tif p.atCRLF() {\n\t\tp.pos += 2\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\treturn p.errorf(\"unexpected text after value\")\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) skipSpaces() {\n\tfor !p.done() && (p.src[p.pos] == ' ' || p.src[p.pos] == '\\t') {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) done() bool {\n\treturn p.pos >= len(p.src)\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) atCRLF() bool {\n\treturn strings.HasPrefix(p.src[p.pos:], \"\\r\\n\")\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) atNewline() bool {\n\treturn !p.done() && (p.src[p.pos] == '\\n' || p.atCRLF())\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) errorf(format string, args ...any) error {\n\tline := 1 + strings.Count(p.src[:p.pos], \"\\n\")\n\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"%w: line %d: %s\", ErrSyntax, line, fmt.Sprintf(format, args...))\n}\n\nfunc isBareKeyByte(c byte) bool {\n\treturn (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') || (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || c == '-' || c == '_'\n}\n\n// isDisallowedControl reports whether c is a control character TOML forbids in\n// strings and comments. Tab is the only control character it allows. Line breaks\n// are excluded here because each caller decides whether a line break is legal.\nfunc isDisallowedControl(c byte) bool {\n\treturn (c < 0x20 && c != '\\t' && c != '\\n') || c == 0x7f\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":15,"oldLines":7,"newStart":15,"newLines":7,"lines":[" "," // Decode reads a TOML document from r and returns its tagged-value model."," // Each top-level key maps to {\"type\", \"value\"} with the value as a string.","-// Only top-level key/value pairs with string values are decoded so far.","+// Only top-level key/value pairs with string, boolean, integer, or float values are decoded so far."," func Decode(r io.Reader) (map[string]any, error) {","   data, err := io.ReadAll(r)","   if err != nil {"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false,"contentNotInModelContext":true},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01XbjwomPGdncLmShwXoSU2c","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

toml\n\nimport (\n\t\"errors\"\n\t\"math\"\n\t\"reflect\"\n\t\"strings\"\n\t\"testing\"\n)\n\n// scalarValueDoc is the tagged model a document `n = <value>` must decode to.\nfunc scalarValueDoc(kind, value string) map[string]any {\n\treturn map[string]any{\"n\": map[string]any{\"type\": kind, \"value\": value}}\n}\n\nfunc TestDecodeBooleans(t *testing.T) {\n\ttests := []struct {\n\t\tname  string\n\t\tinput string\n\t\twant  string\n\t}{\n\t\t{name: \"true\", input: \"true\", want: \"true\"},\n\t\t{name: \"false\", input: \"false\", want: \"false\"},\n\t}\n\tfor _, tt := range tests {\n\t\tt.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {\n\t\t\tdoc, err := decodeString(\"n = \" + tt.input + \"\\n\")\n\t\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"Decode(%q) error = %v, want nil\", tt.input, err)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\twant := scalarValueDoc(\"bool\", tt.want)\n\t\t\tif !reflect.DeepEqual(doc, want) {\n\t\t\t\tt.Errorf(\"Decode(%q) = %v, want %v\", tt.input, doc, want)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t})\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestDecodeIntegerForms(t *testing.T) {\n\ttests := []struct {\n\t\tname  string\n\t\tinput string\n\t\twant  string\n\t}{\n\t\t{name: \"zero\", input: \"0\", want: \"0\"},\n\t\t{name: \"positive\", input: \"42\", want: \"42\"},\n\t\t{name: \"explicit plus\", input: \"+99\", want: \"99\"},\n\t\t{name: \"negative\", input: \"-17\", want: \"-17\"},\n\t\t{name: \"underscore groups\", input: \"1_000_000\", want: \"1000000\"},\n\t\t{name: \"signed underscores\", input: \"-1_2\", want: \"-12\"},\n\t\t{name: \"hex\", input: \"0xDEADBEEF\", want: \"3735928559\"},\n\t\t{name: \"hex lowercase with underscore\", input: \"0xdead_beef\", want: \"3735928559\"},\n\t\t{name: \"octal\", input: \"0o755\", want: \"493\"},\n\t\t{name: \"octal with underscore\", input: \"0o7_7\", want: \"63\"},\n\t\t{name: \"binary\", input: \"0b11010110\", want: \"214\"},\n\t\t{name: \"binary with underscore\", input: \"0b1101_0110\", want: \"214\"},\n\t\t{name: \"largest signed 64-bit\", input: \"9223372036854775807\", want: \"9223372036854775807\"},\n\t\t{name: \"smallest signed 64-bit\", input: \"-9223372036854775808\", want: \"-9223372036854775808\"},\n\t\t{name: \"largest hex signed 64-bit\", input: \"0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF\", want: \"9223372036854775807\"},\n\t\t{name: \"hex smallest signed 64-bit\", input: \"0x8000000000000000\", want: \"-9223372036854775808\"},\n\t}\n\tfor _, tt := range tests {\n\t\tt.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {\n\t\t\tdoc, err := decodeString(\"n = \" + tt.input + \"\\n\")\n\t\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"Decode(%q) error = %v, want nil\", tt.input, err)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\twant := scalarValueDoc(\"integer\", tt.want)\n\t\t\tif !reflect.DeepEqual(doc, want) {\n\t\t\t\tt.Errorf(\"Decode(%q) = %v, want %v\", tt.input, doc, want)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t})\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestDecodeFloatForms(t *testing.T) {\n\ttests := []struct {\n\t\tname  string\n\t\tinput string\n\t\twant  string\n\t}{\n\t\t{name: \"simple\", input: \"3.14\", want: \"3.14\"},\n\t\t{name: \"zero\", input: \"0.0\", want: \"0\"},\n\t\t{name: \"negative zero\", input: \"-0.0\", want: \"-0\"},\n\t\t{name: \"explicit plus\", input: \"+1.5\", want: \"1.5\"},\n\t\t{name: \"negative\", input: \"-0.5\", want: \"-0.5\"},\n\t\t{name: \"underscore\", input: \"6_626.0\", want: \"6626\"},\n\t\t{name: \"exponent\", input: \"1e6\", want: \"1e+06\"},\n\t\t{name: \"signed exponent\", input: \"6.626e-34\", want: \"6.626e-34\"},\n\t\t{name: \"capital exponent with plus\", input: \"5E+22\", want: \"5e+22\"},\n\t\t{name: \"zero prefixed exponent\", input: \"1e05\", want: \"100000\"},\n\t\t{name: \"zero integer part with exponent\", input: \"0e0\", want: \"0\"},\n\t\t{name: \"fraction with exponent\", input: \"-2.5e3\", want: \"-2500\"},\n\t\t{name: \"smallest denormal\", input: \"5e-324\", want: \"5e-324\"},\n\t\t{name: \"largest finite\", input: \"1.7976931348623157e308\", want: \"1.7976931348623157e+308\"},\n\t\t{name: \"positive infinity\", input: \"inf\", want: \"inf\"},\n\t\t{name: \"explicit plus infinity\", input: \"+inf\", want: \"inf\"},\n\t\t{name: \"negative infinity\", input: \"-inf\", want: \"-inf\"},\n\t\t{name: \"not a number\", input: \"nan\", want: \"nan\"},\n\t\t{name: \"signed not a number\", input: \"+nan\", want: {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01UUyjwWVb4ULQrcU9yveSeJ","type":"tool_result","content":"The \"test\" command runs the test cases.\n\nThe way toml-test works is that for every test case it executes a \"decoder\"\ncommand, which reads TOML from stdin and then outputs JSON describing that TOML\n(or returns an error if it thinks the TOML isn't valid). Encoder tests work the\nsame except in reverse: it reads JSON and transforms that to TOML.\n\nThere are three types of tests:\n\n    valid      Valid TOML that the decoder command should describe as JSON.\n    invalid    Invalid TOML files that should be rejected with an error.\n    encoder    JSON that the encoder command should transform to TOML.\n\n\u001b[1mImplementing a decoder:\u001b[0m\n\n    A decoder reads TOML data from stdin and outputs a JSON description to\n    stdout and exits with code 0. If the TOML data is invalid, it must exit\n    with code 1. It's recommended to write an error message to stderr.\n\n    An example in pseudocode:\n\n        toml_data = read_stdin()\n\n        parsed_toml = decode_toml(toml_data)\n\n        if error_parsing_toml():\n            print_error_to_stderr()\n            exit(1)\n\n        print_as_json_description(parsed_toml)\n        exit(0)\n\n    Details of the JSON format is explained below in \"JSON description\".\n\n\u001b[1mImplementing an encoder:\u001b[0m\n\n    An encoder is the reverse of a decoder; it reads a JSON description from\n    stdin converts that to TOML.\n\n    An example in pseudocode:\n\n        json_data = read_stdin()\n\n        json_description = decode_json(json_data)\n\n        print_as_toml(json_description)\n        exit(0)\n\n\u001b[1mJSON description\u001b[0m\n\n    TOML is described with JSON as follows:\n\n    - TOML tables correspond to JSON objects.\n    - TOML arrays correspond to JSON arrays.\n    - TOML values correspond to a JSON object of the form:\n      {\"type\": \"{TOML_TYPE}\", \"value\": \"{TOML_VALUE}\"}\n\n    In the above, TOML_VALUE is always a JSON string (even for integers or\n    bools), and TOML_TYPE may be one of: string, integer, float, bool,\n    datetime, datetime-local, date-local, or time-local.\nShell cwd was reset to /mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/Toml/runs/20261014.124728/build/toml","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"f869f945-d43e-4f9b-bd86-3059116a99c8","uuid":"45c239dd-7bfd-4166-b57a-ffc5d0cc9650","timestamp":"2026-10-14T13:02:30.357Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"The \"test\" command runs the test cases.\n\nThe way toml-test works is that for every test case it executes a \"decoder\"\ncommand, which reads TOML from stdin and then outputs JSON describing that TOML\n(or returns an error if it thinks the TOML isn't valid). Encoder tests work the\nsame except in reverse: it reads JSON and transforms that to TOML.\n\nThere are three types of tests:\n\n    valid      Valid TOML that the decoder command should describe as JSON.\n    invalid    Invalid TOML files that should be rejected with an error.\n    encoder    JSON that the encoder command should transform to TOML.\n\n\u001b[1mImplementing a decoder:\u001b[0m\n\n    A decoder reads TOML data from stdin and outputs a JSON description to\n    stdout and exits with code 0.
